A bike boulevard between Uptown and downtown

Proposed routes, directional controls and measured pavement

Open printable overview ↗

Each marker is an encounter on the selected route in its direction. An all-way STOP has a green A; ordinary STOPs are red S. A red ? is a known STOP whose all-way status remains unassessed. Hollow light markers are map/model inferences, not directed visual confirmations.

Click a control for its source, confidence, dates and available evidence. This is a dated route audit, not a survey of every sign in the city.

Connections that need resolving

Purple dashed segments mark the original dismount links. Some use road centerlines as approximate sidewalk locators. They must not be read as legal wrong-way bicycle links. The proposed boulevard needs clear, usable connections here.

About 203 m of campus paths have no measured pavement readings, including about 46 m mapped as gravel. Cycling access and pedestrian priority need explicit treatment in a public route design.

Pavement and control evidence

Bumpy Roads roughness: under 3 is smoother; 3–6 mixed; 6–9 rough; 9+ very rough. Gray dashes mean limited or missing readings. Nearby roadway observations are not transferred to campus paths or dismount links.

Controls combine OpenStreetMap, Mapillary machine detections followed by directed visual checks, Google Street View and scoped local observations. Dates differ by location; a reviewed historical image does not guarantee today's arrangement.

The offline street geometry and all displayed route/control data are embedded in this file. Optional online tiles contact OpenStreetMap. No recorded private ride tracks are included.
